audits.title: 757. Impact of a Sepsis Improvement Team with Prospective Audit and Feedback on SEP-1 Core Measure Adherence in an Urban Community Hospital
audits.intervention: Sepsis improvement team (ID physician and nurse) running prospective audit and feedback within 48 hours of admission, with education and corrective actions; order sets, checklists and EMR alerts already in place.
audits.other_findings: Commonest failures in both groups were initial and repeat lactate.
audits.citation: Mena Lora A, Sim S, Spencer S, Coleman Y, Krill C, Takhsh E, et al.. 757. Impact of a Sepsis Improvement Team with Prospective Audit and Feedback on SEP-1 Core Measure Adherence in an Urban Community Hospital. Open Forum Infect Dis. 2019;6(Suppl 2):S338-S338.

audits.title: An audit of compliance with the sepsis resuscitation care bundle in patients admitted to A&E with severe sepsis or septic shock.
audits.standard: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 6-hour resuscitation care bundle
audits.setting: A&E department of a district general hospital (Kent and Sussex Hospital, Tunbridge Wells)

cycle1.result: Overall compliance with the 6-hour bundle 19%; arterial lactate done 100% of the time; only just over half received an appropriate fluid challenge; antibiotic administration very slow.

audits.other_findings: Recommendations included improving the A&E track and trigger system, the prescribing doctor administering antibiotics, and staff education.
audits.citation: Baldwin LN, Smith SA, Fender V, Gisby S, Fraser J. An audit of compliance with the sepsis resuscitation care bundle in patients admitted to A&E with severe sepsis or septic shock. Int Emerg Nurs. 2008;16(4):250-256. doi:10.1016/j.ienj.2008.05.008. PMID: 18929343.

audits.title: Protocol Adherence for Severe Sepsis and Septic Shock Management in the Emergency Department; a Clinical Audit.
audits.standard: Surviving Sepsis Campaign protocols and British Royal College recommendations
audits.setting: Emergency department, Imam Hossein Hospital, Tehran

cycle1.result: Mean resident knowledge score 5.07 +/- 1.78; adherence for urine output, CVP monitoring, inotropes, transfusion, IV antibiotics, fluids and high-flow oxygen was low.

audits.intervention: Training workshops for emergency medicine residents.

cycle2.result: Mean knowledge score 8.17 +/- 1.31; some measures improved clinically but not statistically.

audits.other_findings: Adherence remained disappointingly low for several measures.
audits.citation: Alavi-Moghaddam M, Anvari A, Soltani Delgosha R, Kariman H. Protocol Adherence for Severe Sepsis and Septic Shock Management in the Emergency Department; a Clinical Audit. Emerg (Tehran). 2017;5(1):e16. PMID: 28286823.

audits.title: Use of a Clinical Audit System in Implementing Surviving Sepsis Campaign Guidelines in Patients With Peritonitis.
audits.setting: Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research, Puducherry (patients with generalised peritonitis)

cycle1.result: Overall bundle compliance 9.2%; IV bolus, CVP-guided fluids and inotropes 100%.

audits.intervention: Audit-based feedback in PDSA cycles with multidepartment input to modify practice

cycle2.result: Overall bundle compliance 64.7%; significant improvement in blood cultures before antibiotics, antibiotics within three hours and serum lactate.

audits.other_findings: Four audit cycles were run; reasons for non-compliance were explored by questionnaire.
audits.citation: Valiveru RC, Cherian A, Srinivasan K, Maroju NK. Use of a Clinical Audit System in Implementing Surviving Sepsis Campaign Guidelines in Patients With Peritonitis. Cureus. 2021;13(6):e15961. doi:10.7759/cureus.15961. PMID: 34211817.

audits.title: Improving the management of sepsis in a district general hospital by implementing the 'Sepsis Six' recommendations.
audits.standard: Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines and Sepsis Six bundle; antibiotics, IV fluids and oxygen within one hour of initial assessment
audits.setting: 130-bed district general hospital (ED and general wards), South Canterbury DHB

cycle1.result: 16 of 55 (29%) had antibiotics, IV fluids with or without oxygen within 1 hour; lactate measured in 10 (18%); blood cultures in 18 (33%); urine output monitoring in 15 (27%); 35% received 4-6 bundle elements.

audits.intervention: Sepsis Six pathway and posters; education workshops for ED staff, junior doctors and ward nurses; designated sepsis assistants; laminated Sepsis Six photo on ED phlebotomy trolleys; request for an extra ED consultant.

cycle2.result: 25 of 40 (63%) had antibiotics, fluids with or without oxygen within 1 hour; lactate 10 (25%); blood cultures 25 (63%), 96% before antibiotics; urine output monitoring 17 (43%); 66% received 4-6 bundle elements.

audits.other_findings: A 3-month re-audit (n = 71) showed 52% within 1 hour. Time to clinician review did not improve (47 to 44 minutes) and in-hospital mortality rose from 2% to 10%, possibly due to winter re-audits.
audits.citation: Kumar P, Jordan M, Caesar J, Miller S. Improving the management of sepsis in a district general hospital by implementing the 'Sepsis Six' recommendations. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u207871.w4032. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u207871.w4032. PMID: 26734403.

audits.title: A quality improvement project to improve the Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) sepsis bundle compliance rate in a large healthcare system.
audits.standard: CMS sepsis bundle (SEP-1) compliance; aim to improve from 30% to 40% within 1 year
audits.setting: 20 acute care hospitals, Banner Health system, Arizona

cycle1.result: Mean compliance 25.8% (monthly range 16-31%); baseline rate for SPC 28.5%.

audits.intervention: Revised sepsis standardised clinical practice and system-wide education; computerised decision support to reflex-order repeat lactate and prompt lactate and blood cultures when antibiotics ordered; pharmacy made first-time IV antibiotic orders stat.

cycle2.result: Mean compliance 34.6% in the second 6 months (p<0.0001), peaking at 42%; 31.8% after CMS changed specifications in July 2016 (p<0.019 vs baseline).

audits.other_findings: Most commonly missed elements were repeat lactate (30%), blood cultures (19%) and antibiotics (16%); the improvement was not sustained after the CMS specification change. Total denominator over 12 months was 1850 patients.
audits.citation: Raschke RA, Groves RH, Khurana HS, Nikhanj N, Utter E, Hartling D, et al.. A quality improvement project to improve the Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) sepsis bundle compliance rate in a large healthcare system. BMJ Open Qual. 2017;6(2):e000080. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2017-000080. PMID: 29450277.
